fieldMarks: Largest ground squirrel in its range; 430-540 mm body, 600-800 g
Mottled: grayish brown in front, grayish black behind, with indistinct wavy brown-and-black markings
Large head and eyes; ears project above the head; long bushy tail, 73-82% of body length
Resembles a tree squirrel more than a typical ground squirrel
behavior: Diurnal; peaks midday in spring, fall and winter, morning or late afternoon in summer
May hibernate at higher elevations, active all year at lower ones
Colonial, with maternal groups and a dominant male
Eats nuts, seeds, grain, berries, roots, green plants, cactus, invertebrates and meat
habitat: Rocky places: cliffs, canyons, hillsides, arroyos, talus, old buildings and stone walls; not usually open plains, deserts or high montane forest.
range: Southeastern Nevada, Utah, Colorado and extreme western Oklahoma south through the southwestern US into Mexico; sea level to 2,900 m.
